facts.heading: Exhausted as per GP suggestion
facts.content: Daniel feels exhausted, describing it as running on fumes.
facts.evidence: She said I look exhausted, and she's right, I am.

facts.heading: Burnout started in October

facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October.

facts.evidence: We lost a big client, and half the team got moved onto the rescue plan

facts.heading: Working late into the night
facts.content: Daniel works from his desk at seven and continues answering messages until ten at night.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night.

facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours.

facts.heading: Wakes at three in morning

facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights

facts.evidence: His hands shake, and he's slower, and he gets frustrated.

facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds.

facts.heading: Sister Hannah lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about care

facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.content: When his sister Hannah asks how he is, Daniel tells her he is fine.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine.

facts.evidence: some days I sit in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before I go in, because I can't face it.

facts.evidence: She did blood tests, and they were all normal.

facts.content: Daniel's GP suggested he talk to someone, but Daniel said he hadn't got time.
facts.evidence: asked if I'd thought about talking to someone. I said I hadn't got time.

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked therapy session
facts.content: Claire, Daniel's girlfriend, booked the therapy session.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire.

facts.heading: Girlfriend concerned about Daniel
facts.content: Claire is concerned because she feels she is done watching Daniel disappear.
facts.evidence: She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend, because I always say no.

facts.heading: Daniel worries about Dad
facts.content: Daniel worries that his Dad might need something if he is away.
facts.evidence: And Dad might need something.

facts.heading: Last time properly off
facts.content: Daniel cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: I can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Ran 10km for six years
facts.content: Daniel used to run ten kilometres every Saturday morning for six years.
facts.evidence: I ran. Ten kilometres every Saturday morning. I'd done it for six years.

facts.heading: Stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago because his legs felt like lead.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs felt like lead, and then I just never went back.

facts.heading: Feels loss of self from running
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself since stopping running.
facts.evidence: Like I've lost a part of myself.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails

facts.evidence: he sends emails at eleven at night

facts.heading: Boss expects early replies
facts.content: Daniel's boss expects an answer to emails before breakfast.
facts.evidence: and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Daniel answers all boss emails
facts.content: Daniel answers every email from his boss, even when he is in bed.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed.

facts.heading: Fear of being seen as uncommitted
facts.content: Daniel is afraid his boss will think he is not committed if he doesn't answer.
facts.evidence: That he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss in spring
facts.content: Daniel is afraid of being let go due to a restructuring in the spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.content: Daniel thinks part of him would be relieved if he lost his job, but then he would feel horrible about being relieved.
facts.evidence: I think part of me would be relieved, and then I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Has a mortgage
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Reports flat and irritable moods
facts.content: Daniel reports feeling mostly flat and irritable.

facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.content: Daniel has experienced episodes like this a couple of times. One occurred on the train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: A couple of times. Once on the train to Manchester.

facts.heading: Has not told Claire about episodes
facts.content: Daniel has not told Claire about these episodes.
facts.evidence: I haven't told anyone about it, not even Claire.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears that he is losing his mind and not coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Coffee intake amount
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee per day.
facts.evidence: Coffee, probably. I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Uses wine in evenings
facts.content: Daniel has started drinking wine in the evenings to distract himself. He drinks two or three glasses.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wine causes uneasiness
facts.content: Daniel feels uneasy after drinking wine, and he wakes up at three AM anyway.
facts.evidence: Uneasy. It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Relief from sharing feelings
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief after sharing his feelings, like putting down a bag.
facts.evidence: A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.
